chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ghalib ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'and their shadows by the morning and the evening,' he said: 'It is the supplication before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and it is a time of acceptance.'

key_terms.الْآصالِ: Evening supplications or prayers offered in the late afternoon/evening
key_terms.الْغُدُوِّ: Morning supplications or prayers offered in the early morning
key_terms.سَاعَةُ إِجَابَةٍ: A time of acceptance (when du'a is likely to be answered)
key_terms.قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: Before the rising of the sun (Fajr time)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-ghuduww wa al-asal' in Surah Ar-Ra'd according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the Quranic phrase 'al-ghuduww wa al-asal' not merely as a temporal marker, but as the specific window for supplication before sunrise and before sunset, highlighting these moments as times when prayers are readily accepted. This interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual potency of the dawn and dusk hours, linking the physical act of prayer with the metaphysical concept of divine responsiveness during these transitional times of day.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Ghalib Bin Abdullah,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [13:15] and their shadows (too) by the morning and the evening. Heasws said: ‘It is the supplication before the emergence of the sun, and before its setting, and it is the time for the Answering’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Asbat from Ghalib ibn ‘Abd Allah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, ‘All in the heavens and the earth prostrate themselves before Allah, either of their own free will or by force, just as do their shadows in the mornings and evenings,’ [13:15] the Imam said, ‘This is prayer before sunrise and before sunset and it is the hour in which prayers are heard.’”
